messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy paused — parity check failed for secret key `model_cache_key` between staging and prod. Block reason: trailing whitespace in staging value. See /deploy/logs/2769991009 :warning:

sam: Wait, trailing whitespace? That's... embarrassing. How did that happen?

maya: Ops rotation script trimmed whitespace only when run with `--normalize=true` which we ran for prod but skipped for staging earlier this week.

ryan: Do we roll back the image or fix the secret in staging and continue? Change window closes in ~30m.

leo: Quick diff from the vault export:
```diff
- model_cache_key: "abc123"
+ model_cache_key: "abc123 "  # trailing space present in staging export
```

amanda: If we rollback now we'll delay a bunch of teams. Is it safe to normalize staging to match prod? Any risk of incompatible tokens?

maya: Normalizing (trim) is safe for this key. It only affects cache namespace. No re-encryption needed — KMS metadata unchanged.

ryan: Are there any downstream consumers that might have already written caches with the trailing-space key? If so, normalization might cause a cache miss spike.

sam: Good point. We should expect a small spike in cache misses for that service for a few minutes. We can do a quick canary in prod if we patch staging then push canary 1 replica.

leo: Alternatively, we can patch the runtime to apply `.trim()` when reading the env var. That avoids a vault change but requires a tiny code change and a fast canary.

amanda: Which is faster? Vault secret update and backfill or runtime normalization + redeploy?

maya: Vault update is ~5m + audit + CI for the rotation job. Runtime patch is a tiny PR but needs a build and canary deploy (20–30m). Given the window, vault edit is faster.

oncall-bot: Reminder — emergency change process requires a post-change runbook entry and slack #incidents notification if performed outside planned maintenance.

sam: Ok proposed plan: 1) Patch vault secret in staging to remove trailing space (quick rotation), 2) rerun parity check, 3) allow deploybot to continue with canary limited to 1 pod, watch cache miss metric (redwood.cache.hits/misses) and latency. If spike > 5% for 10m, rollback.

ryan: I'll own the canary watch. If we see >10% increase in 5m, rollback to previous image.

leo: I'll open a quick vault rotation PR (link: https://vault.internal/pull/452) and add a one-line runbook note.

amanda: Also add a line to the release notes: "Hotfix: normalized model_cache_key value in staging; parity check required. No code changes."

maya: I'll add an automated normalization check to the rotation job so future runs won't diverge. PR: https://infra/pulls/2987

deploy-bot: Awaiting parity recheck after secret rotation. Release remains paused.

sam: Thanks. Once deploy-bot clears, proceed with canary per plan. Update this thread when parity passes.
